clue.text: Aid to driver's prospect, we'll engage one cracking whips

indicators.note: cracking means breaking apart, so the word whips is broken up and rearranged
to engage is to take in or hold, so the first word holds the rest within it

blocks.note: the pronoun we, taken as written, as the outer shell
one is the article A
the letters of whips, rearranged

explanation.surface: A coach driver's warning that someone will step in to stop a whip-cracking scene.
explanation.walkthrough: WE (the 'we' of we'll) holds A plus a jumble of WHIPS: W(A SHWIP)E.
explanation.definitionFit: A wash-wipe is the windscreen washer and wiper system that keeps a motorist's forward view clear.

clue.text: Doings at Davos? Tense porter's employed with gains around (12, two words)

indicators.note: employed suggests letters being put to work in a new arrangement
around means the word for gains wraps about the jumbled letters

blocks.note: first part of WINS, gains, which is split to hold the rest
T for tense plus the letters of porter's, rearranged
last letter of WINS closes the shell

explanation.surface: A tense hotel porter is hired on good pay at a Swiss resort.
explanation.walkthrough: T (tense, grammar abbreviation) joins PORTERS in the anagram, all inside WINS. Davos is a Swiss ski resort, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiing, bobsleigh and similar activities are what visitors to the Alpine resort do, an example-style definition.

clue.text: Dog, one breed that's trained with measure of dash

indicators.note: something trained is shaped into a new form, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: one is A; with breed the letters are rearranged
an en is a printer's measure, the width of an en dash

explanation.surface: A dog of one breed is trained to show some dash.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aberdeen terrier is another name for the Scottish terrier, a breed of dog.

clue.text: Instrument for chopping a slate suitable for one's rockery

blocks.note: a sax is a slater's hammer for cutting roofing slates
taken as written
a slate is a kind of roofing tile

explanation.surface: A tool for cutting slate is recommended for building a garden rockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' suggests music and the saxophone, but here SAX is the slater's chopper.
explanation.definitionFit: Saxatile describes plants and creatures living among rocks, which suits the stony setting of a rock garden.

clue.text: Last of a casserole used as starter – to avoid this?

definitions.text: Last of a casserole used as starter – to avoid this?

indicators.note: the final letter is taken from the end and put at the front of the word

blocks.note: a stew is a casserole

explanation.surface: Serving leftover casserole as a first course is a thrifty habit.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the last letter of A STEW to the front to get WASTE; read whole, the clue describes thriftily serving up leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Serving up leftovers is a way to avoid throwing food away, which is the squandering the answer names.

clue.text: Producer of ferrous sulphate modified skin shade

indicators.note: modified means changed, so the letters of skin are put in another order

blocks.note: the letters of skin, rearranged
a shade or tint of colour

explanation.surface: A chemical compound causes a change in skin colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Inkstone is a mineral containing iron sulphate, once used in making ink, so it is a source of the salt.

clue.text: Saint Simon? (Could be a catch)

blocks.note: first meaning: the apostle, a saint
second meaning: forename of the singer-songwriter surnamed Simon
third meaning: a variant spelling of pawl, a ratchet's catch

explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: the apostle, the singer of Simon and Garfunkel, and a Chambers variant of pawl, a pivoted catch on a ratchet.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to both the apostle and the American musician, and is also a variant spelling for a mechanical catch.

clue.text: To go through exercises run quickly round area

indicators.note: round means the word for quickly goes about the area letter

blocks.note: physical education
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run
vite is a musical direction meaning quickly
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Gym exercises: running fast in circles around a space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run quickly' reads as one phrase but splits into R and VITE, which goes round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Perviate is a rare verb meaning to pass through or penetrate a way, from Latin pervius.

clue.text: Some real barren mounts, bleak in the Cairngorms?

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following words is taken
in a down entry, mounting means climbing upwards, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A description of the bare, bleak Scottish mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cairngorms are Scottish mountains, flagging a Scots word: blae means bleak or livid blue-grey.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect the word means livid or bleak and sunless, so it suits the Highland setting.

clue.text: Wretched waste in the sea

blocks.note: first meaning: miserable, low in spirits
second meaning: to squander money
third meaning: the open sea, as in 'out into the' one

explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: down in spirits, to squander (Chambers' 'blue' one's money), and 'the ...' for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour word also means depressed, as a verb means to spend recklessly, and names the sea in a set phrase.

clue.text: Old dance? Assume a spree is wrong for it

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so the letters must be arranged afresh

blocks.note: all twelve letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: Going on a binge would be the wrong approach to a stately old dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The passemeasure was a stately Italian dance of the 16th century, related to the passamezzo.

clue.text: What's smoked oyster I've trimmed, included in Spanish dish?

explanation.walkthrough: A native is a cultivated British oyster; remove I'VE from NATIVE to leave NAT, then put it inside PAELLA.

clue.text: Bond girlfriend no longer enthralled by union

a former partner

explanation.definitionFit: A nexus is a connection or link, the same sense as a bond tying things together.

clue.text: Malay craft fixed oars up, not old

not old tells us to drop the letter standing for old

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: O is the abbreviation for old: remove it from OARS UP and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Praus (or proas) are fast Malay sailing boats, so the plural fits craft.

clue.text: Feature of nude, informal? Artist added in touches

indicators.note: added in means put inside, so the artist goes within the other word

blocks.note: a slang word for breasts, a feature of a nude
Royal Academician

explanation.definitionFit: A trait can mean a stroke or touch, as of a pen or brush, so the plural matches touches.

clue.text: Eastern vessel in trouble, second going for quays

indicators.note: in trouble means disturbed or upset, so the letters are disordered
going means departing, so the abbreviation for second leaves

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Eastern ship is in difficulty and a second is heading for the quays.
explanation.walkthrough: E plus VESSEL loses one S, and the six letters left are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A levee is an embankment or landing place on a river, so quays are a fair synonym.

clue.text: Expectant woman's affliction? Reduced energy immobilizes end of pregnancy

indicators.note: reduced means cut down to its abbreviation, a single letter
end of points to the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: E is the symbol for energy
clamps holds fast, as a wheel clamp immobilizes a car
the final letter

explanation.surface: A worrying complication: low energy that leaves a woman unable to move late in pregnancy.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclampsy, or eclampsia, is a dangerous convulsive condition that can strike a woman during pregnancy.

clue.text: Chinese communist exchanging extremes for religion

indicators.note: the first and last letters trade places with each other

blocks.note: a follower of Chairman Mao

explanation.surface: A Chinese Party member swaps one extreme belief for a religion.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the outer letters of MAOIST, M and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Taoism is the Chinese philosophical and religious tradition founded on the teachings of Laozi.

clue.text: Signifying 'doer', one brought in untangled a tangle

indicators.note: brought in means taken inside, so the letter for one joins the group
untangled means sorted out, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is called in to sort out a mess, as a doer would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Untangled a tangle' looks circular, but tangle is just the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar an agential suffix such as -er marks the agent, the one who performs the action.

clue.text: Silence one noisy row? Increasingly tricky

blocks.note: the hushing sound
the Roman numeral
F is forte, loud in music
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: Someone tries to quieten a loud argument, and things get trickier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noisy row' reads as a quarrel, but it splits into F (forte) and TIER, a row of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Shifty means evasive or deceitful, so the comparative means more so.

clue.text: Noblewoman is bent, in grip of chronic fatigue

blocks.note: first letter of ME, myalgic encephalomyelitis

second letter of ME

explanation.walkthrough: ME is myalgic encephalomyelitis, known as chronic fatigue syndrome.
explanation.definitionFit: A marchese is an Italian marquise, the wife of a marchese or a lady of that rank.

clue.text: Spain in grip of opulent foreign empire

E is the international vehicle code for Spain
rest of RICH

explanation.definitionFit: Reich is the German word for empire or realm, as in the Third Reich.

clue.text: Cheer in school for what Scottish climber attempts?

explanation.definitionFit: Grahams, like Munros, are classified Scottish summits that walkers aim to bag.

clue.text: Woven lisle, new purchase by retailer

clue.text: Sliver of noisette consumed red?

clue.text: Fabric mark? A firm's upset with this
